title: Matter and Energy Transfer in Organisms Review Test
description: Review practice for matter and energy transfer in organisms.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains where most matter for plant growth comes from?
questions.questionText: Which statement best explains where most matter for plant growth comes from?
options: carbon dioxide and water are rearranged into sugar and plant materials
questions.correctAnswer: carbon dioxide and water are rearranged into sugar and plant materials
questions.explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide and water during photosynthesis to make sugars and build materials.

questions.prompt: Which model best connects photosynthesis and food webs?
questions.questionText: Which model best connects photosynthesis and food webs?
options: light -> producers make sugars -> consumers get food molecules
questions.correctAnswer: light -> producers make sugars -> consumers get food molecules
questions.explanation: Producers make food molecules that support food webs.

questions.prompt: A sealed plant chamber loses carbon dioxide in bright light. Which claim is best supported?
questions.questionText: A sealed plant chamber loses carbon dioxide in bright light. Which claim is best supported?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a reactant in photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: Which process releases usable energy from food molecules in cells?
questions.questionText: Which process releases usable energy from food molecules in cells?
questions.explanation: Cellular respiration releases usable energy from food molecules.

questions.prompt: A student says, "Energy cycles through ecosystems exactly like matter." What is the best correction?
questions.questionText: A student says, "Energy cycles through ecosystems exactly like matter." What is the best correction?
options: Matter cycles, while energy flows and changes form.
Matter disappears but energy has mass.
Food webs show no energy movement.
questions.correctAnswer: Matter cycles, while energy flows and changes form.
questions.explanation: Matter cycles; energy flows through systems.

questions.prompt: A food web starts with grass, then grasshoppers, then frogs. What happens to energy?
questions.questionText: A food web starts with grass, then grasshoppers, then frogs. What happens to energy?
options: Energy starts with frogs and becomes sunlight.
Energy flows from grass to grasshoppers to frogs.
Energy does not move through feeding.
questions.correctAnswer: Energy flows from grass to grasshoppers to frogs.
questions.explanation: Energy transfers as organisms eat food molecules.

questions.prompt: Which evidence best supports that plants need light for sugar production?
questions.questionText: Which evidence best supports that plants need light for sugar production?
options: Leaves in bright light produce more starch than leaves kept in darkness.
questions.correctAnswer: Leaves in bright light produce more starch than leaves kept in darkness.
questions.explanation: Starch evidence can show sugar production related to light.

questions.prompt: A student claims animals do not depend on photosynthesis. Which evidence best challenges this?
questions.questionText: A student claims animals do not depend on photosynthesis. Which evidence best challenges this?
options: Animals eat plants or organisms that ate plants, gaining food molecules from producers.
questions.correctAnswer: Animals eat plants or organisms that ate plants, gaining food molecules from producers.
questions.explanation: Food webs connect animals to producers directly or indirectly.

questions.prompt: Which cause/effect chain explains low oxygen in a crowded yeast flask?
questions.questionText: Which cause/effect chain explains low oxygen in a crowded yeast flask?
options: more cells -> more respiration -> more oxygen use
more cells -> less need for food
questions.correctAnswer: more cells -> more respiration -> more oxygen use
questions.explanation: Respiring cells use oxygen to release energy from food molecules.

questions.prompt: Why is sunlight not considered matter for plant growth?
questions.questionText: Why is sunlight not considered matter for plant growth?
options: Sunlight has more mass than soil.
Sunlight is energy, not atoms used to build plant structures.
Sunlight is made of plant cells.
questions.correctAnswer: Sunlight is energy, not atoms used to build plant structures.
questions.explanation: Matter is made of atoms; sunlight provides energy.

questions.prompt: A model says: sugar -> usable energy + carbon dioxide + water. Which process is modeled?
questions.questionText: A model says: sugar -> usable energy + carbon dioxide + water. Which process is modeled?
questions.explanation: Respiration breaks down food molecules and releases usable energy.

questions.prompt: Which data pattern would support that respiration increases with activity?
questions.questionText: Which data pattern would support that respiration increases with activity?
options: active cells use oxygen faster than resting cells
questions.correctAnswer: active cells use oxygen faster than resting cells
questions.explanation: Higher oxygen use can indicate more cellular respiration.

questions.prompt: How do decomposers connect to matter cycling?
questions.questionText: How do decomposers connect to matter cycling?
options: They break down dead material and return matter to the environment.
They stop food webs from using matter.
questions.correctAnswer: They break down dead material and return matter to the environment.
questions.explanation: Decomposers recycle matter from dead organisms and wastes.

questions.prompt: Which model revision improves: plant -> animal?
questions.questionText: Which model revision improves: plant -> animal?
options: light -> plant sugars -> animal food molecules -> respiration in animal cells
questions.correctAnswer: light -> plant sugars -> animal food molecules -> respiration in animal cells
questions.explanation: A stronger model traces food molecules and energy release.

questions.prompt: A student says plants get all their food from soil. Which response best uses evidence?
questions.questionText: A student says plants get all their food from soil. Which response best uses evidence?
options: Plants do not need carbon dioxide.
Plants make sugars from carbon dioxide and water using light energy; soil supplies some minerals.
questions.correctAnswer: Plants make sugars from carbon dioxide and water using light energy; soil supplies some minerals.
questions.explanation: Plants make food molecules through photosynthesis, while soil can provide minerals.
